Summary:
The data source is a commentary on the 2016 “Expert Survey on Progress in AI”. It reports machine-learning researchers’ forecasts for high-level machine intelligence (HLMI) under different question framings, their perceived probabilities of extremely bad outcomes (including human extinction), and their attitudes toward AI-safety research. Key empirical findings are (1) large framing effects that systematically shift timeline estimates, (2) wide variance among experts, and (3) broad but under-resourced support for value-alignment research. These findings motivate interventions such as improving survey methodology, establishing progress-tracking infrastructures, and increasing dedicated AI-safety funding.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[82]  
The instructions were followed closely: all identified causal paths are represented from risks through intermediate node categories to interventions; nodes use merge-friendly, context-rich names; every node connects into the single fabric; no intervention connects directly to a risk. Confidence is reduced slightly by the narrative style of the source (no explicit section headings) and by limited quantitative detail for edge strength.

Inference strategy justification:
Moderate inference (edge confidence 1–2) was applied only where the paper implies but does not explicitly state causal links (e.g., uncertain timelines exacerbating extinction risk). All other links draw directly on reported survey results or well-known alignment arguments quoted in the text.

Extraction completeness explanation:
All substantive claims, methods, findings, and proposals appearing in the text have been decomposed into 18 nodes (≈15 nodes/5k words target) and connected through 24 edges, yielding a fully-connected knowledge fabric covering (a) misalignment-driven extinction risk and (b) socio-economic disruption risk from automation.

Key limitations:
1. The source provides no direct experimental validation of proposed interventions; maturity levels are therefore ≤ 3.  
2. Section references in rationales are approximate (“Survey results”, “Main interesting results”) because the web post lacks formal headings.  
3. Socio-economic disruption receives less granularity because the text focuses on HLMI safety.
